inspections.sourceIdentity: W3C PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
inspections.locator: §2.1 PROV Core Structures — derivation between entities.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That a later entity may be recorded as derived from an earlier one, giving a traceable chain between versions of a work.
inspections.boundary: Supports expressing a lineage. It does not establish that a cited chain is correct, that a citation is warranted, or that any particular citation practice is standard.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Carried forward into Tranche 16 via Tranche 15: same source, same locator, same claim scope. Originally inspected as tr13-src-004.

inspections.sourceIdentity: PubMed Central, Author Manuscripts in PMC

inspections.accessBasis: United States government service, freely accessible.

inspections.supportedClaimScope: That an author manuscript is the version peer reviewed and accepted by a journal, including changes made during peer review but generally excluding copyediting and stylistic edits.

inspections.sourceIdentity: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
inspections.locator: Control AU-2 (Event Logging), items a and b.
inspections.accessBasis: United States government publication, freely available.

inspections.supportedClaimScope: That auditability begins with identifying which event types a system is capable of logging in support of the audit function, and coordinating that logging with the parties who need audit-related information.

inspections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
inspections.accessBasis: Published by the BIPM Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: Reference-only. Bounded original summary; the definition is not reproduced verbatim into artifacts.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That calibration is a two-step operation: first establishing a relation between quantity values with measurement uncertainties provided by standards and the corresponding indications with their uncertainties, then using that relation to obtain a measurement result from an indication.
inspections.boundary: This is measurement calibration of an instrument against a standard. It does not define calibration of a probabilistic forecast, which is a different concept sharing the word. A page on forecast calibration must not cite this definition, and this source establishes nothing about model confidence.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Carried forward into Tranche 16 via Tranche 15: same source, same locator, same claim scope. Originally inspected as tr15-src-101.

inspections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
inspections.locator: §2.41 (6.10), definition of metrological traceability, with Note 1.
inspections.accessBasis: Published by the BIPM Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: Reference-only. Bounded original summary; the definition is not reproduced verbatim.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That metrological traceability is a property of a measurement result: the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.
inspections.boundary: This is traceability of a measurement to a reference standard. It is not provenance of a document, lineage of a citation, or an audit trail of a system, all of which share the word. A page about record traceability must not cite this definition.
inspections.relationshipToEarlier: Same document as the calibration inspection in Tranche 15, read at a different definition.

inspections.accessBasis: United States government publication, freely available.
inspections.reuseBasis: US government work; bounded original summary with attribution.
inspections.supportedClaimScope: That incident response is treated as part of cybersecurity risk management rather than a standalone activity, and is distributed across the Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions.
inspections.boundary: Recommendations and considerations, not a reporting obligation. It sets no disclosure deadline, names no regulator, and does not establish when an incident must be reported to anyone.
